This specification covers testing requirements, construction requirements, tolerances, and drawing interpretation for wire assemblies, cable assemblies, and harness assemblies. This is a multiple variation specification (indication of permitted or prohibited substitution). See Articles 2.0 and 4.0.
The drawing designation indicates whether substitution is permitted or prohibited for the terminal, terminal attachment method, and terminal insulator called out on the assembly drawing.

A non-insulated terminal, insulated according to Paragraph 5.5, may be substituted for a pre-insulated terminal. The terminal shall accept the same wire size, stud or screw size, tool clearance, and envelope width as the pre-insulated terminal. The terminal thickness shall not be less than the pre-insulated terminal.
1E2358C - Processing prohibits substitution. Adherence to Paragraphs 5.5.1 and 5.6.3 is optional.

1E2358D - Processing and testing harness assemblies with 4 Wire, 10 Mbps Ethernet. Reference paragraph 5.4.8, 5.9 and 10.3. Unless otherwise specified, if the 467-2859 multiconductor is used on a harness, the requirements of 1E2358D shall be followed. When 1E2358D is present on a drawing, the requirements for 1E2358A shall also apply.
1E2358E - Processing High voltage low current cable assemblies. Reference Article 6.0.

1E2358F - Processing and testing harness assemblies with 2 Wire, 100 Mbps Ethernet. Reference paragraph 5.4.9 through 5.4.13, 5.9, 10.4 and 10.5. Unless otherwise specified, if the 489-6290 multiconductor is used on a harness, the requirements of 1E2358F shall be followed. When 1E2358F is present on a drawing, the requirements for 1E2358A shall also apply.

5.4.1 Crimp terminals shall not suffer any damage or deformations caused by or during any part of the harness assembly build process which could affect the correct mating or separation forces of single or multi-pole connectors.

The terminal shall be crimped to the wire using tooling and procedures specified by the terminal manufacturer. This includes crimp location, crimp height, and crimp width. If the terminal drawing allows for multiple manufacturers, preference should be given to those with complete tooling and application specifications. Aluminum locator dies are not allowed for use in the Pico applicators. Alternative tooling and procedures may be used when approved by the terminal design control and the Global Purchasing Segment Supplier Development Engineer (SDE) after agreed upon electrical and mechanical testing to be performed by the supplier.

5.4.3.1 Solid Contact Terminal Crimp Criteria - (A) Visible strands in inspection hole. (B) Proper crimp detents. (C) Visible strands at end of barrel. (D) No flayed wires. (E) No bird cage wires. (F) No visible strands in inspection hole. See Figure 4.

When the total insulation area of the wires and the terminal insulation crimp areas are not compatible, removal of the insulation crimp is acceptable.

Using network cable stripper, remove the jacket to the (A) dimensions in table regardless if heat shrink tubing is specified on drawing. Maintain the factory cable twist rate, do not modify the twist rate.

Note: Use caution when removing jacket. If conductor insulation is nicked or slightly cut, discard and start with fresh wire. If there is any damage to the conductor, hence the insulation has been compromised, discard and start with fresh wire.
Unless otherwise specified, install 125-7874 adhesive lined dual wall heat shrink tubing or equivalent to (B) dimension, unless noted on the drawing to build cables without dual wall heat shrink.

Center the heat shrink tubing on the end of the stripped jacket. The heat shrink tubing is added to maintain the factory twist rate and prevent water and contaminants from getting inside the cable jacket and changing the characteristics of the Ethernet wire. The heat shrink tubing will want to slide from the larger jacket diameter down to the unjacketed wires. Process controls should be in place to manage the heat shrink location during assembly. Allow to cool, do not dunk heat shrink in water to cool.
The heat shrink to jacket and individual wires shall meet the sealing requirement as identified in section 10.7.1. The SDE will review the harness manufacturer's process controls.

Straighten wires to prepare for installing terminal assemblies, and to make the wires equal length for the trimming process. If the drawing calls out for no heat shrink, then the (C) measurement shall be from the end of the stripped jacket.
Care should be taken during the untwisting process, so that untwisting of the factory twist rate behind the heat shrink does not occur, as this would be difficult to inspect/detect.

Some automated equipment is available and should be considered for production use. Untwisting of the factory twist will degrade the Ethernet signal quality, and shall be avoided. The SDE will review the harness manufacturer's process controls.

The 2 terminated lead lengths shall be within 1mm max of each other (untwisted, straightened, cut to length and terminated) as measured from the end of the dual wall heat shrink or jacket as shown above. Uneven wire lengths can cause noticeable signal quality degradation.

Caterpillar recommends the use of dual cut, strip and crimp tooling to handle the needed process controls to deliver a good quality Ethernet segment. This dual cut, strip, untwist, crimp tooling is capable of delivering matching wire lengths, proper insulation removal, untwist, terminal alignment and quality dual crimps.

Some semi-automated tooling is available from TE to hold wire positions, cut, strip and simultaneously crimp both terminals. This tooling should be considered to provide improved process controls, but is not required if supplier process satisfies all special characteristics and is approved by the SDE.

When crimping the wires, it is important that each Ethernet wires be oriented to match the connector pinout for the specific circuit (per the harness drawing). Wires terminating into a 2 position receptacle should orient the white wire with the blue stripe on the left side of the blue wire. Failure to properly position the Ethernet wires prior to crimping will require the wires to be twisted before inserting the contacts into the connectors, making assembly difficult and can result in degraded signal quality. Do not spot solder the 2 wire Ethernet terminals.

Crimping process should be done with each wire aligned to the other. Keep the wires parallel as you crimp each wire will help with inserting the contacts into the connector. Rotated terminal indicated (G) will misalign both sides of mating area within the connectors.

Tilting of terminals indicated (F) will have negative impact on the Ethernet signals. If for one reason or the other, a terminal gets a poor crimp, start the process all over again. Terminals not being within the (F) dimension can be caused by not assembling the terminal position assurance (TPA).

If a lubricant is desired, isopropyl alcohol shall be used. There shall not be a separation in the twisted pair (this is also referred to as an eye), where the wires do not maintain the factory twist, and open in the distance between the wires. During the heat shrink process, ensure that the adhesive does not get in between the wires. Separation of the wires will decrease signal quality, and will be rejected. That is why maintaining a factory twist, means that if there is a separation in the 2 wires (or an open eye), that this is cause for rejection. An example is shown below. Keeping the Ethernet twisted pair with mild bends will help to avoid the chance of sharp bends that will degrade Ethernet signal quality.
